primary_diagnosis_treated: Chronic kidney disease stage 5 / End‑stage renal disease
nice_guideline_used: NICE NG203 (Chronic kidney disease: assessment and management)

medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each dose titration
medications.purpose: Control hypertension, reduce proteinuria and slow CKD progression
medications.nice_justification: NG203 first‑line ACE‑I/ARB for CKD with hypertension or ACR ≥ 30 mg/mmol; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1‑2 weeks

medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction (CKD is a risk‑equivalent; patient has IHD and diabetes)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends a statin for all CKD patients for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 1 g orally three times daily (≈0.5 mmol/kg/day for a 70 kg adult)
medications.duration: Until serum bicarbonate ≥22 mmol/L, then review
medications.purpose: Correct metabolic acidosis (CO₂ 20.8 mmol/L) which contributes to bone disease and muscle wasting
medications.nice_justification: NG203 advises treating metabolic acidosis in CKD stage 5 with oral bicarbonate when CO₂ <22 mmol/L

medications.dose: 800 mg orally three times daily with meals
medications.duration: Until serum phosphate within target range (0.8‑1.5 mmol/L), then review
medications.purpose: Control hyperphosphataemia and reduce secondary hyperparathyroidism
medications.nice_justification: CKD‑MBD management per NICE CKD guidelines (NG203 recommends monitoring phosphate, calcium, PTH and using binders as needed)

medications.duration: Until PTH within target range, then review
medications.purpose: Treat secondary hyperparathyroidism of renal origin
medications.nice_justification: NICE CKD‑MBD guidance (NG203) recommends active vitamin D when PTH is markedly elevated

medications.dose: 5,000 IU subcutaneously once weekly (dose adjusted to weight and Hb response)
medications.duration: Until hemoglobin 10‑12 g/dL is achieved, then review every 4 weeks
medications.purpose: Treat anaemia of chronic kidney disease
medications.nice_justification: NICE CG186 (Anaemia in CKD) recommends ESA when Hb <10 g/dL and iron stores are replete

contraindications.reason: Accelerates CKD progression and causes fluid retention; patient has eGFR 5.4 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: Use acetaminophen for pain if needed

contraindications.reason: eGFR <30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: Consider dose reduction of other glucose‑lowering agents; insulin may be required

contraindications.reason: Increases risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury; patient already receiving an ACE‑I
contraindications.alternative: Continue single ACE‑I (Ramipril) as per NG203

contraindications.reason: Nephrotoxic and contraindicated in advanced CKD
contraindications.alternative: Use alternative mood stabiliser (e.g., valproate) if required

contraindications.reason: eGFR < 30 mL/min/1.73 m² – high risk of contrast‑induced nephropathy
contraindications.alternative: If imaging required, use low‑osmolar contrast with adequate hydration and N‑acetylcysteine prophylaxis

contraindications.reason: NICE TA775 recommends use only when eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m²; patient eGFR 5.4 mL/min/1.73 m²
contraindications.alternative: No SGLT2 inhibitor; focus on ACE‑I, BP control, and dialysis planning

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium not provided – must be measured before starting Ramipril and repeated 1‑2 weeks after initiation.
Liver function tests not provided – required before initiating Atorvastatin.
Serum phosphate, calcium, PTH values not available – needed to confirm need for sevelamer and calcitriol.
Full anemia work‑up (Hb, ferritin, TSAT) not available – required before starting epoetin alfa.
Blood pressure reading not recorded – assume hypertension uncontrolled; monitor after ACE‑I initiation.
Allergy status unknown – verify no hypersensitivity to ACE‑I, statin, sevelamer, calcitriol, or epoetin.
Vaccination status (influenza, pneumococcal, hepatitis B) not documented – arrange per NICE CG182.
Weight/BMI confirmed obese (BMI ≥ 30) – advise weight‑management program.
Patient awaiting kidney transplantation – coordinate medication timing with transplant team (e.g., hold ACE‑I 24‑48 h pre‑op).
treatment_summary: Start low‑dose Ramipril and Atorvastatin as first‑line therapy for hypertension, proteinuria and cardiovascular risk (NG203). Correct metabolic acidosis with oral sodium bicarbonate, manage phosphate and secondary hyperparathyroidism with sevelamer and calcitriol, and treat CKD‑related anaemia with epoetin alfa once labs confirm need. Avoid contraindicated agents (NSAIDs, metformin, ACE‑I + ARB, lithium, IV contrast, SGLT2 inhibitors). Monitor renal function, electrolytes, liver enzymes and relevant CKD‑MBD parameters per NICE recommendations, and provide lifestyle advice and vaccination updates.
